theater: 青海湟水鄯州城與北岸渡口

battle.name: 鄯州之戰
battle.theater: 青海湟水鄯州城與北岸渡口
battle.brief: 景祐二年（1035），湟水中游的鄯州（今青海樂都）捲入青藏高原東北部重新劃界的衝突：控制鄯州、青唐一線的吐蕃諸部，與西面壓進來的党項夏州勢力在城郊與渡口一帶交鋒，宋廷只以封授招撫居中。卡面的希臘火不在這個內陸戰場上，同期可與之對照的東方燃燒武器是猛火油櫃、火矢與發火飛石。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 一〇三五年的鄯州之戰，發生在湟水中游的鄯州城一帶，即今青海省海東市樂都區。正史對這一役的記載相當零散，只在《資治通鑑》卷二百八十四所記景祐二年（1035）前後的邊事，以及《宋史·吐蕃傳》《宋史·夏國傳》的殘文與《遼史》興宗本紀的附記裡留下片段，交戰序列與雙方名號歷來聚訟不一。可以確定的是，交鋒的一方是控制鄯州、青唐與湟水渡口一線的吐蕃諸部，其中混有吐谷渾餘部、漢地流民與歸附的羌人部族，平日以牧業立身，遇戰則以騎兵為主力；另一方是從西北壓進來的党項夏州勢力，即李德明病故後由李元昊接手的靈州部，此時尚未建國稱帝，正沿河西走廊東段向湟水上游推進。橫在雙方之外的是宋朝：自大中祥符元年（1004）起，宋廷冊封鄯州一帶的首領唃廝囉為敦煌郡王、檢校太尉，又接連派僧侶與使者入蕃傳經通好，希望以封賞和茶馬交易換取邊界安寧，卻始終沒有在湟水流域駐紮大軍；遼朝此時正忙於收拾與高麗的邊界糾紛與西域哈剌契丹的壓力，興宗雖於重熙四年因蕭太后病逝而親政，也沒有餘力深入青海。於是這是一場雙方都靠自己的力量、而大國只在幕後觀望的邊境衝突。
countriesEn: The Battle of Shanzhou of 1035 was fought around the walled town of Shanzhou on the middle reaches of the Huangshui, in what is today Ledu District of Haidong in Qinghai. The written record of the engagement is thin. It survives only in fragments: the frontier notices in Zizhi Tongjian volume 284 covering the second year of the Jingyou era (1035), the surviving text of the Tibetan and Western Xia biographies in the History of Song, and a short note in the Xingzong annals of the History of Liao. The order of the fighting, and even the names of the parties, have long been disputed. What can be established is this. One side was made up of the Tibetan tribes holding Shanzhou, Qingtang and the fords of the Huangshui, a population that mixed Tibetan groups, the remnants of the Tuyuhun, Han colonists and surrendered Qiang; in peacetime they lived on herding, and in war the bulk of their strength was mounted. The other side was the Tangut power based on Xiazhou and Lingzhou, which had just passed from Li Deming to Li Yuanhao and, though it had not yet proclaimed an empire, was pushing eastward along the western corridor toward the upper Huangshui. Outside both stood the Song. From the first year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era (1004) the court had been granting titles to the local ruler, Chos grub being made Dunhuang junwang and jianjia taiwei, and it sent monks and envoys across the plateau again and again to preach and keep relations, hoping to buy quiet along the frontier with titles and tea-for-horses trade, yet it never garrisoned a major force in the Huangshui valley. The Liao was then occupied with settling disputes with Goryeo and with the pressure of the Qara Khitai in Central Asia; although the Xingzong emperor took personal rule in the fourth year of the Chongxi era after the dowager died in 1035, he had no strength to march into Qinghai. In the end this was a border clash fought by the local powers themselves, with the great empires only watching from the wings.
people: 一〇三五年在湟水兩岸活動的人，多數姓名已經散失，只能從零星記載中拼出輪廓。黨項方面，李德明在景祐初年病故，長子李元昊接下靈州與夏州的地盤，這年三十出頭，尚未稱帝建元，卻已在整頓兵馬、收編部眾、經營原州與環州一線的據點，鄯州之役正落在他在西北整合的關鍵時刻；如何約束族內各支、如何與母族和姻姓勢力分配牧地，是那幾年最麻煩的內政。吐蕃方面，鄯州一線的首領是唃廝囉一系，這位吐蕃出身的首領在大中祥符年間接受宋朝的封號，統轄西至涼州、東至河州，擁有數以萬計的牧帳與馬群，節制諸部、維持與宋廷的封貢往來；他身邊有漢地傳入的僧侶與書吏充任譯人，鄯州城內也聚居著一批漢地移民與行商，度支、詞訟與譯事多由這批人經手。1035年正值這位強勢首領在位的中期，他的諸子與部族首領已各據一方、爭奪牧地與驛站，為日後的分裂埋下伏筆。宋廷方面，仁宗年紀尚輕，宰府與三司一意避免在西北另開戰場，對鄯州的介入仍以封授、賜物、遣使為主，只在僧人往來中略帶調停之意。值得注意的是，多數指揮官的姓名並沒有留下來，記載裡只剩「以蕃騎追之」「夜引兵至城下」「遁去數百騎」這類片段。
peopleEn: The names of most of the men who fought along the Huangshui in 1035 have been lost, and their outlines can be reconstructed only from scattered notices. On the Tangut side, Li Deming had died in the early Jingyou years, and his eldest son Li Yuanhao, then in his early thirties, inherited the lands of Lingzhou and Xiazhou. He had not yet proclaimed himself emperor, but he was already regularising his troops, gathering in the branches of his clan and holding posts along Yuanzhou and Huanzhou, and the clash at Shanzhou fell exactly in the middle of that consolidation in the northwest; how to hold the various lines of the clan in check, and how to divide pastures with the maternal and marriage alliances, was his most delicate domestic business in those years. On the Tibetan side, the ruler of the Shanzhou line was the house of Chos grub, a man of Tibetan origin who had accepted Song titles in the Dazhong Xiangfu years, whose authority ran west to Liangzhou and east to Hezhou, and who commanded tens of thousands of herding households and droves of horses, keeping the tribes in order and sustaining the tributary and exchange relations with the Song court. Han monks and clerks from the interior served him as interpreters, and a small population of Han settlers and itinerant traders lived in the town, with accounts, litigation and translation largely handled by them. The year 1035 fell in the middle of this strongman's rule, while his sons and the tribal chiefs had already begun to hold their own ground and to dispute pastures and relay stations, a fault line that would soon split the region. On the Song side the emperor was still young, and the chancellery and the Board of Revenue were determined to open no new front in the northwest, so the court's involvement at Shanzhou remained limited to conferring titles, bestowing gifts and sending envoys, with a faint mediating intent carried by the travelling monks. Notably, the commanders' names have not survived: the record preserves only phrases such as he pursued them with Tibetan riders, he led his men by night to the foot of the wall, and several hundred riders withdrew.
kits: 卡面上的希臘火是拜占庭帝國的招牌裝備。相傳它由君士坦丁堡的工匠卡利尼科斯在七世紀末試成，灌在銅管裡的噴射式燃燒劑，最初用在與阿拉伯人的地中海爭奪中，敘利亞、埃及沿岸的戰艦與攻城戰都有它的身影，拜占庭編年史作者狄奧多西及其續編者都描述過那種在海面與城牆前騰起、連水都澆不熄的火。然而鄯州之戰是一場青藏高原東北部的高原內陸戰役，希臘火並不在現場，這一點必須說清楚；能與卡面對照的，是同一時期東方的同類技術。猛火油櫃在中原與河西已有長期使用，《太平御覽》所引的舊籍裡可以見到以膏液灌器焚燒的記載，侯景圍臺城時亦有以猛火油車焚燒守軍的記載；唐人杜佑《通典》與李筌《太白陰經》則把火藥箭、發火飛石與猛火油櫃並列為當時最完整的燃燒與爆破手段，明代《武備志》更直接把猛火油與西洋所傳的希臘火相提並論，視為同一類東西。落到鄯州戰場上的實際器械則要樸素得多：蕃部與党項的騎兵用角弓與短骨箭，步卒用長標槊與木盾，披札甲或皮甲，腳蹬高靿靴在碎石與凍土上衝鋒；攻城一方備有撞車、飛石、繩梯與灌了猛火油的陶罐陶甕，防守一方靠唐代留下的邊州城郭、甕城與拒馬硬撐。糧秣靠馬群自帶與牛羊隨軍，趕著驢隊的隊商負責運鹽運茶。
kitsEn: The Greek fire on the card face is the signature weapon of the Byzantine Empire. It is said to have been perfected by an artisan of Constantinople named Kallinikos in the late seventh century: a projected burning mixture pumped through a copper tube, first used in the struggle over the Mediterranean against the Arabs, appearing in naval actions and in assaults along the Syrian and Egyptian coasts, and described by the Byzantine chronicler Theophanes and his continuators as a fire that rose over sea and rampart and could not be quenched by water. The Battle of Shanzhou, however, was a land campaign on the northeastern plateau of the Tibetan highlands, and the Greek fire was not on the field; that has to be said plainly. What can be set against the card face is the equivalent Eastern technology. Oil-fire syringes had been in use in the Chinese interior and in Hexi for a long time; older works quoted in the Taiping Yulan describe vessels filled with oily liquid and set alight, and there is a record of carts of burning oil used against the defenders when Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City. Tang authors such as Du You's Tongdian and Li Quan's Taibai Yinjing list fire arrows, flying stones that burst into flame, and oil-fire syringes together as the most complete set of burning and blasting devices of the age, and the Ming Wubeizhi goes further, identifying menghuoyou with the Western Greek fire as the same class of thing. The actual equipment at Shanzhou was far plainer. Tibetan and Tangut riders used composite bows of horn and sinew with short bone-tipped arrows; footmen carried long spears and wooden shields, wearing lamellar or hide armour and stepping in high-soled boots over scree and frozen ground. The attacking side brought battering rams, stone-throwers, rope ladders and ceramic jars and pots filled with burning oil, while the defenders relied on the frontier town walls left by the Tang, the barbican and cheval-de-frise. Food and fodder came with the horses themselves and with cattle and sheep driven along, while mule trains carried the salt and the tea.
tactics: 湟水河谷是這場戰鬥的舞臺。河谷在樂都一帶被兩側山脊夾住，水面寬處不過數十步，道路貼著水邊延伸，車隊只能單列通行，一側受阻，整條線便要癱瘓。蕃部在這裡的優越處是熟悉地形、熟悉草場：守城時以城門、甕城和山頭的哨位互相支援，一旦逼退敵人便不追，任其沿河谷退去，乾燥季節則派小股騎兵沿山脊繞到敵後，專打糧隊與哨所；冬春苦寒，冰雪封山，人馬難行，多半選擇夏秋開打。党項那一方則完全是另一套辦法：輕騎出發、人馬自備乾糧，不打算攻城，只求速戰速決，往往在蕃部騎兵巡邏的空檔從山口或河灣突然切下來，縱騎衝散隊形，掠走馬匹與牲口便走，若遇不利即散入戈壁，絕不戀戰。糧道是他們真正的目標：切斷靈州方向到鄯州的通道，蕃部就必須在沒有外援的情況下獨自撐住。漢地僧人與使者則在兩邊往來，試圖以封號、賜物和佛經勸說蕃部收兵，也試圖把宋廷安撫之意傳到党項耳邊。
tacticsEn: The Huangshui valley was the stage of this clash. Near Ledu the river is hemmed in by ridges on both sides, the water is only a few dozen paces wide in places, and the road runs tight along the bank, so a wagon column can pass in single file; if one stretch is blocked, the whole line chokes. The tribesmen's advantage here was intimate knowledge of the ground and of the pastures. In defence they supported one another from the gates, the barbican and the lookout posts on the hillsides, and once they had thrown the enemy back they did not pursue, letting him fall away along the valley; in the dry season they sent small bodies of horsemen round along the ridges to get behind the enemy and hit the supply columns and the pickets. Winter and early spring are bitterly cold, snow closes the passes, horses and men cannot move, so the fighting was generally left to summer and autumn. The Tangut side worked on an entirely different logic: light cavalry, dry rations carried on the horse, no intention of storming anything, only speed. They would cut in from a mountain gap or a bend of the river during the hours when the tribal patrols were elsewhere, gallop through and break the enemy's order, drive off horses and cattle, and go; if the day went against them they scattered into the gravel desert and never stood and fought. Their true objective was the supply line: cut the road from Lingzhou to Shanzhou and the tribes would have to hold out with no outside help. Han monks and envoys moved between the two sides, trying to talk the tribes back with titles, gifts and Buddhist texts, and trying to carry the Song court's message of pacification to the Tanguts as well.
data: 留下數字的地方不多，可以核的只有幾項。時間上，景祐二年即西元1035年，與遼的重熙四年同年。地理上，湟水是黃河上游的支流，全長約一百五十公里，源頭在湟源一帶的雪水與泉流，自西向東流經西寧、樂都，最後在蘭州附近匯入黃河；鄯州城所在的樂都在湟水東岸，距離湟州治所西寧約八十至一百公里，距離涼州治所武威約三百至四百公里，離最近的大宋邊州還在四百里之外，援兵確實難以指望。地形上，樂都海拔約兩千一百米，河谷段在兩千上下，高原風大、日照強、冬季嚴寒而乾燥，適宜作戰的窗口是夏秋。兵員方面，現存記載沒有給出可信的數目；按當時邊州衝突的常態，一方拉出數千騎、上萬騎並不奇怪，但那是量級而不是本役的實數，不可當作統計。損失、俘獲與耗糧同樣無從核實。倒是物資流向留下痕跡：宋廷以茶、鹽、絲織品與銀器換取蕃部的馬匹與毛皮，鹽是這一帶最硬的硬貨，驢隊與牛車把鹽、茶、糧運進河谷，戰事一起，最先斷的就是這些隊商。
dataEn: Little of the arithmetic survives, and only a few items can be checked. In time: the second year of the Jingyou era, that is 1035 CE, the same year as the fourth year of the Liao's Chongxi era. In geography: the Huangshui is a tributary of the upper Yellow River about 150 kilometres long, fed by snow and springs around Huangyuan, running west to east past Xining and Ledu, and joining the Yellow River near Lanzhou. Ledu, where the town of Shanzhou stood, lies on the eastern bank of the Huangshui, roughly 80 to 100 kilometres from Xining, the seat of Huangzhou, and some three to four hundred kilometres from Wuwei, the seat of Liangzhou, with the nearest Song frontier prefecture still some four hundred li beyond that, so reinforcements were genuinely hard to count on. In terrain: Ledu stands at about 2,100 metres above sea level, the valley running near two thousand, with hard winds, strong sunlight and dry severe winters, which leaves summer and autumn as the usable window for campaigning. In numbers of men: the surviving record gives nothing that can be trusted. A few thousand riders, or ten thousand, on one side would be unremarkable for a frontier clash of this kind, but that is a scale and not a figure for this battle, and it must not be passed off as a statistic. Losses, prisoners and consumption of grain are equally unverifiable. What does leave a trace is the flow of goods: the Song exchanged tea, salt, silk and silver plate for the horses and furs of the plateau, salt being the hardest currency in the district, and mule trains and ox-carts brought salt, tea and grain into the valley, so when the fighting started the first thing to be cut was these caravan teams.
cause: 打起來的原因有多層。最深的一層是唐末留下的真空：吐蕃帝國在九世紀中葉崩解，河湟一帶再沒有一個能號令全區的政權，唐末張議潮一度收復涼州、河湟，卻守不住成果，鄯州、青唐、涼州、河州遂各由大大小小的蕃部與豪族分據，彼此靠盟約、婚姻和互市維持平衡，誰先打破平衡，誰就要付出代價。第二層是党項的擴張。李德明在景祐初年病故，李元昊接位後整合族內各支，把勢力從夏州、靈州往西推，涼州與湟水一帶的牧地、鹽井和商路正是他需要的東西；與蕃部在鄯州撞上並非偶然，而是兩條勢力線在同一條河谷裡必然要擠在一起。第三層是宋朝的政策。宋廷對西北的基本方針是守禦與羈縻，不想在河湟重開戰場，所以對唃廝囉一系一路加封進爵、賜物通好，希望用名義上的羈縻換取邊界安寧；可當蕃部內部分裂、党項又步步進逼時，名義上的羈縻擋不住實際的搶奪，於是宋朝在1035年仍不得不以派官、遣僧、賜物的方式去維持秩序，只是始終沒有投入主力。
causeEn: There were several layers of reason for the fighting. The deepest was the vacuum left by the late Tang. The Tibetan empire had collapsed in the middle of the ninth century, and no authority in the river-and-plateau region could give orders to the whole area ever since; Zhang Yichao recovered Liangzhou and Haidong for a time at the end of the Tang but could not hold the gain, so Shanzhou, Qingtang, Liangzhou and Hezhou came to be held by great and small tribes and local magnates who kept the peace among themselves by alliance, marriage and mutual trade. Whoever broke that balance first would pay for it. The second layer was Tangut expansion. Li Deming died in the early Jingyou years; after Li Yuanhao took over he consolidated the branches of the clan and pushed westward from Xiazhou and Lingzhou, and the pastures, salt wells and caravan roads of Liangzhou and the upper Huangshui were exactly what he needed. Running into the tribes at Shanzhou was not an accident but the inevitable consequence of two lines of force squeezing into the same valley. The third layer was Song policy. The court's basic line in the northwest was defence and control rather than a new campaign in the river lands, so it went on conferring titles and sending gifts to the line of Chos grub, hoping to exchange a nominal bond of control for quiet on the frontier. But once the tribes split among themselves and the Tanguts pressed forward step by step, nominal bonds of control could not hold off real seizure, and so in 1035 the Song still had to keep order by sending officials, monks and gifts, though it never committed its main force.
impact: 這一役沒有改變青海的政治版圖：鄯州仍在吐蕃諸部手中，河谷的門戶關係與牧場分配照舊，宋朝也沒有因此取得任何據點。它的意義在別處。第一，它把1030年代河湟地區的權力真空擺到了明面上——名義上有宋、遼兩朝在周邊觀望，實際上沒有人能替當地做主，鄯州這樣的地方就是各方都想要、又各自守不住的空隙。第二，它是党項勢力膨脹的一個刻度：西夏正式建國還要等到1038年，可是在建國之前，党項人已經在湟水與河西的門口試過刀鋒，兩年後宋夏戰爭爆發時，北宋對西北邊防的脆弱已經被這場衝突提前暴露。第三，它加速了吐蕃方面的內部瓦解：唃廝囉的諸子與部族首領各據一方、互相爭奪牧地與驛站，等到1042年他本人一死，鄯州所在的這塊地方便迅速分裂成若干互相攻伐的小政體，把原本還算穩固的屏障變成了麻煩。這三件事湊在一起，構成日後熙寧年間北宋經營熙河、一步一步把青海東北部拉進中原秩序的遠因。
impactEn: This engagement did not change the political map of Qinghai. Shanzhou remained in the hands of the Tibetan tribes, the pattern of control over the valley's gates and pastures stayed as it was, and the Song gained no foothold from it. Its significance lies elsewhere. First, it laid the power vacuum of the 1030s in the Huangshui region bare: with the Song and the Liao watching from the edges and nobody able to decide matters on the spot, a place like Shanzhou was a gap that every party wanted and none could hold. Second, it was a measure of Tangut strength. The Western Xia state would only be proclaimed in 1038, but before the proclamation the Tanguts had already tried the edge of their sword at the gateway of the Huangshui and of Hexi, and when the Song-Xia war broke out two years later, the fragility of the Song's northwest defences had already been exposed by this clash. Third, it accelerated the internal dissolution of the Tibetan side. The sons of Chos grub and the tribal chiefs each held their own ground and fought over pastures and relay stations, and when their father died in 1042 the land around Shanzhou broke up quickly into a number of small states that attacked one another, turning what had been a fairly solid screen into a nuisance. Taken together, these are the remote causes of the Song's later work in the Xining era on the Xíhé district, which drew the northeastern corner of Qinghai step by step into the order of the Central Plains.
result: 結果一項，現存文獻說得含糊。沒有材料顯示鄯州城被攻破或被攻下，多數說法認為這一役以蕃部保住城池、党項退回靈州方向而收場；即使有短暫的易手，時間也不長，因為雙方都沒有能力長期在外地作戰。實際損失同樣無從核算，能推測的只是：一方在高原河谷裡遠離本境，補給靠馬群與隨軍牛羊，另一方守在城裡有屯糧與牧場，僵持拖下去先撐不住的必然是遠來的一方。結果還包括一套延續了二十年的局面：鄯州依舊是蕃部與吐谷渾餘部共居的城市，漢地僧侶與使者往來不絕，宋廷繼續以封號和茶馬交易經營這條邊界；党項則退回去收拾內部、準備更大的動作。換句話說，1035年的鄯州沒有勝負可言，只有一場把青藏高原東北部的權力格局推向前一個階段的邊境衝突。
resultEn: On the result the documents are vague. Nothing shows that the town of Shanzhou was stormed or taken; most accounts hold that the engagement ended with the tribes keeping the city and the Tanguts falling back towards Lingzhou, and even if the town changed hands for a moment it did not last, because neither side had the capacity to sustain a campaign far from home. Actual losses cannot be reckoned, and what can be inferred is only this: one side was far from its own country in a high plateau valley, subsisting on horses and on cattle and sheep driven along, while the other held the city with its stored grain and pastures, and in a long stalemate it was the distant invader who would tire first. The outcome also included a situation that would last twenty years. Shanzhou remained a city shared by Tibetan tribes and Tuyuhun remnants, with Han monks and envoys coming and going, and the Song court continued to manage this frontier with titles and tea-for-horse trade; the Tanguts, meanwhile, went back to settle their own internal affairs and prepare something larger. In short, there was no winner at Shanzhou in 1035, only a border clash that pushed the power pattern of the northeastern Tibetan plateau into its next stage.
